headline: Mistakes to Sidestep When Upgrading Your Interior Finishes
articleBody:
Upgrading your interior finishes can dramatically improve your Berkeley or East Bay home, but it's easy to make a few missteps along the way. One common mistake we see is picking finishes in isolation instead of as a coordinated set. You really want everything to work together – the flooring, paint, cabinetry, and fixtures – so your rooms flow beautifully. Choosing a color for the walls without considering how it plays with your new backsplash or existing furniture can lead to a disjointed look.

Another pitfall is selecting sizes or colors that just don't suit the room's proportions. A huge, bold pattern might overwhelm a small space, while a very subtle texture could get lost in a larger one. Always consider the scale of your room. And don't just focus on appearance; upgrading without checking durability, maintenance, or compatibility with existing elements is another frequent mistake. You might love a certain material, but if it's high-maintenance and you're not prepared for that, you'll regret it later. For projects that involve precise alignment across rooms or multiple trades, bringing in a professional like Frasheski Construction can help you avoid these headaches and ensure a cohesive, lasting result.
